ui.lib.arcade.mustPass: You have no legal move — you pass.
ui.lib.arcade.noHint: No useful move left. Draw a card, deal a new row or start over.
ui.lib.arcade.note.2048: Use the arrow keys or swipe to slide every tile. Two tiles with the same number merge into one when they touch. Make a tile equal to the target to clear the level; if no tile can move, you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.note.blocks: Rotate and place the falling pieces to fill horizontal lines; full lines disappear. ← → move, ↑ rotates, ↓ soft drops, Space hard drops, P pauses. Clear the required number of lines to pass the level; if the stack reaches the top, you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.note.breakout: Move the mouse, drag your finger on the field or use ← → to steer the paddle and keep the ball in play. Break every brick to clear the level; bricks with a thick border take two hits. You have 3 lives. Press Space to start or pause.
ui.lib.arcade.note.connect4: You play red and move first. Tap a column to drop a disc; it falls to the lowest empty spot. The first to line up 4 discs horizontally, vertically or diagonally wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.freecell: All cards are face up. Move all 52 cards to the 4 foundations by suit, from A to K. On the tableau, build down in alternating colors. The free cells at the top left hold one card each; how many cards you can move at once depends on the free cells and empty columns. Higher levels have fewer free cells.
ui.lib.arcade.note.gomoku: You play X and move first; the computer plays O. Take turns placing a mark on an empty point of the 15×15 board. The first to get 5 in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.klondike: Move all 52 cards to the 4 foundations by suit, from A to K. On the tableau, build down in alternating colors; only a K can go into an empty column. Tap the face-down pile at the top left to draw. Tap a card and then where you want it, or tap the card again to send it to a valid spot. Levels 1–5 draw 1 card, levels 6–10 draw 3.
ui.lib.arcade.note.match3: Swap two neighboring pieces (tap one then the other, or swipe) to make a line of 3 or more of the same kind; the line pops and the pieces above fall down. Chain reactions multiply your points. Reach the target score before you run out of moves.
ui.lib.arcade.note.minesweeper: Tap a cell to open it. A number shows how many mines are in the 8 cells around it. Flag a suspected mine with a right click, a long press or Flag mode. Tap a number that already has enough flags around it to open the rest quickly. Open every cell without a mine to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.reversi: You play Black and move first. Place a disc so that it traps one or more White discs between it and another Black disc (horizontally, vertically or diagonally); the trapped discs flip to your color. If you have no legal move, you pass. When the board is full, whoever has more discs wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.snake: Steer the snake with the arrow keys, WASD, the buttons below or by swiping. Eat the red food to grow; reach the required length to pass the level. From level 3, hitting a wall ends the game; higher levels add obstacles. Don't bite your own tail.
ui.lib.arcade.note.spider: Build each suit into a run from K down to A on the tableau; a complete 13-card run is removed automatically. Any card can go on a card one rank higher, but only same-suit runs move together. When you're stuck, tap Deal a new row (every column must have cards). Levels 1–3 use one suit, 4–7 two suits, 8–10 four suits.
ui.lib.arcade.shuffled: No moves left — the board was reshuffled.
ui.lib.arcade.noHintFc: No useful move left. Try undoing a few moves or start over.
ui.lib.arcade.wrapOff: K does not link to A
ui.lib.arcade.hintDraw: No pairs left. Click the stock to draw.
ui.lib.arcade.note.blackjack: Play money only — no real money. You start with 500 chips; reach the target chip count within the allowed number of hands to clear the level. Get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. The dealer draws until reaching 17. A blackjack (an ace plus a ten-value card) pays extra. Double: double your bet and take exactly one more card. Split: available when your first two cards have the same value.
ui.lib.arcade.note.videopoker: Play money only — no real money. Choose a bet of 1–5 chips, press Deal to get five cards, click the cards you want to keep, then press Draw to replace the rest. A pair of jacks or better pays. You start with 100 chips; reach the target chip count within the allowed number of hands to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.checkers: You play Red (bottom) and move first. A piece moves one square diagonally forward onto an empty square. If you can jump over an opposing piece you must, and you may keep jumping to capture several pieces. A piece that reaches the far row is crowned king and can move and capture backward too. You lose when you have no pieces or no legal move.
ui.lib.arcade.ckWin: Black has no legal moves — you win.
ui.lib.arcade.ckLose: You have no legal moves — you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.ckMust: You must capture when you can — pick one of the pulsing pieces.
ui.lib.arcade.note.oanquan: A traditional Vietnamese game. The bottom row is yours, the top row is the computer's, and the two ends are the Mandarin squares. Click one of your squares, then choose a direction: all stones in it are picked up and sown one per square. After sowing, if the next square has stones, pick them up and keep sowing; if the next square is empty and the one after it has stones or a Mandarin, you capture it (and keep capturing if another empty square is followed by a loaded one). Stop at a Mandarin square or after two empty squares in a row. A Mandarin is worth 10 points, a stone 1. If your side runs out of stones, 5 of your captured points are sown back. The game ends when both Mandarins are captured; the higher score wins.
ui.lib.arcade.oqWin: Game over — you have more points.
ui.lib.arcade.oqLose: Game over — the computer has more points.
ui.lib.arcade.note.ludo: You play Red; the other colours are played by the computer. Roll the die: you need a 6 to bring a token out of its yard, and a 6 gives you another roll (three 6s in a row loses your turn). Tokens travel clockwise around the board, then turn into the home column of their colour; you need the exact number to reach the finish in the centre. Landing exactly on an opponent's token sends it back to its yard (except on star squares and start squares). The first player to bring all 4 tokens home wins.
ui.lib.arcade.ldWin: All 4 of your tokens are home!
ui.lib.arcade.threeSix: Three 6s in a row — you lose your turn.
ui.lib.arcade.note.pyramid: Clear all 28 cards of the pyramid. Click two free cards (not covered by any card) that add up to 13 (A=1, J=11, Q=12) to remove both; a King is removed alone with one click. The top card of the waste pile can be used too. Click the stock to draw; the number of times you can recycle the waste pile is limited.
ui.lib.arcade.note.tripeaks: Clear all 28 cards of the three peaks. Click a free card that is exactly one rank higher or lower than the card showing on the waste pile (any suit) to move it down. When you are out of moves, click the stock to draw. On the easier levels, a King links to an Ace.
ui.lib.arcade.note.golf: Press on the course, pull back away from where you want to hit (like a slingshot) and release to strike the ball; the farther you pull, the harder the hit. Sink the ball in the hole when it is slow enough; sand slows it down. Each level is a different course with a limited number of strokes.
ui.lib.arcade.hnBad: You cannot place a larger disc on a smaller one.
ui.lib.arcade.fillAll: Please pick a colour for every position.
ui.lib.arcade.note.nonogram: The numbers at the start of each row and column give the lengths of the runs of consecutive filled cells in that line, in order, with at least one empty cell between runs. Click or drag to fill cells; switch to “Mark ✕” to note cells you are sure are empty. Satisfy every clue to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.sokoban: Move the player with the arrow keys/WASD, the buttons below, or by swiping. Push every box onto a goal square (the round dots). You can only push one box at a time and cannot pull, so avoid pushing boxes into corners. Use Undo to fix a bad move.
ui.lib.arcade.note.block10: Pick a piece at the bottom, then click the grid to place it (pieces cannot be rotated). Fill a whole row or column to clear it and score extra points; clearing several lines at once earns a big bonus. Reach the target score to clear the level; if none of the remaining pieces fits, you lose.
ui.lib.arcade.note.dots: Take turns joining two neighbouring dots with a line. Whoever draws the fourth side of a square claims it (in their colour) and moves again. When all lines are drawn, the player with more squares wins. Avoid drawing the third side of a square, or your opponent will take it.
ui.lib.arcade.note.ultimate: The board is made of 9 small tic-tac-toe boards. You play X and go first. The cell you pick inside a small board decides which small board your opponent must play in next (it is highlighted); if that board is already finished, they may play anywhere. Win a small board to claim it; claim three small boards in a row, column or diagonal to win the game.
ui.lib.arcade.note.lights-out: Clicking a cell toggles that cell and its 4 neighbours (on/off). Turn all the lights off. Use Hint to see a cell worth pressing.
ui.lib.arcade.note.fifteen: Slide the numbered tiles into the gap to put them in order 1, 2, 3… with the gap in the bottom-right corner. Click a tile in the same row or column as the gap to slide the whole line; arrow keys also work.
ui.lib.arcade.note.flood-it: Pick a colour to fill the whole area you own in the top-left corner; it swallows neighbouring cells of that colour. Make the entire board one colour within the allowed number of moves.
ui.lib.arcade.note.mastermind: The computer hides a row of colours. Choose a colour for each position, then press Guess. A black peg = right colour in the right place; a white peg = right colour in the wrong place. Crack the code before you run out of guesses.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hanoi: Move all the discs to the last peg. Move only the top disc of a peg each time, and never place a larger disc on a smaller one. Click the source peg, then the target peg.
ui.lib.arcade.note.pipes: Click a tile to rotate the pipe 90°. Connect every pipe into one network with no open ends left (open ends are shown in red).
ui.lib.arcade.note.whack-a-mole: Moles pop up from the holes — click or tap a mole to whack it. Whack enough moles before time runs out. From level 4 there are bombs: hitting one costs you points.
ui.lib.arcade.note.simon: The game plays a sequence of colours and sounds — repeat it in the same order. Each round adds one more step. Remember the required length to clear the level. From level 7 there are 6 pads.
ui.lib.arcade.note.aim-trainer: Targets appear at random and vanish quickly — hit as many as you can. They get smaller and faster. Hit enough targets before more than 5 misses to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.quick-math: Solve in your head as fast as you can: type the answer and press Enter. Each question has a time limit; a wrong answer or timeout costs a life (you have 3). Answer enough questions correctly to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.reaction: Wait for the screen to turn green, then click as fast as you can. Clicking too early is a foul (3 fouls and you lose). Your average over 5 rounds must beat the level’s limit.
ui.lib.arcade.note.pong: Move the mouse, drag your finger or use the ← → keys to control the bottom paddle. Knock the ball past the computer; first to 5 points wins. The ball speeds up with every hit.
ui.lib.arcade.note.space-shooter: Move the mouse, drag your finger or use the ← → keys to steer; your ship fires automatically. Destroy enough enemy ships to clear the level, and avoid collisions and enemy fire. You have 3 lives.
ui.lib.arcade.note.asteroids: ← → rotate the ship, ↑ thrusts, Space fires. Destroy every rock to clear the level; big rocks split into smaller ones. The ship wraps around the screen edges. You have 3 lives.
ui.lib.arcade.note.maze: Use the arrow keys (or swipe, or the buttons) to get from the green dot to the red flag before time runs out. From level 5 the maze is foggy: you only see around you, and visited areas are remembered.
ui.lib.arcade.note.road-cross: Use the arrow keys, swipe or the buttons to hop the frog from bottom to top. Avoid the traffic; from level 5 the upper part is a river, so hop onto the floating logs. Get home 3 times to clear the level. You have 3 lives.
ui.lib.arcade.note.flappy: Tap the play area, press Space or ↑ to flap. Fly through the gaps between pipes without touching a pipe, the ground or the ceiling. Higher levels have narrower gaps and faster flight.
ui.lib.arcade.note.runner: Tap the play area, press Space or ↑ to jump over cacti; hold ↓ to duck under high birds (or jump over low ones). Run far enough to clear the level. The speed keeps rising.
ui.lib.arcade.note.kalah: You play the bottom row, the computer the top; the big pit on the right is your store. Click a pit to pick up all its seeds and sow them counter-clockwise, one per pit (skipping your opponent’s store). If your last seed lands in your store you move again; if it lands in an empty pit on your side opposite a pit with seeds, you capture those seeds. When one side is empty, the other side’s seeds go to its owner’s store; the bigger store wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.snakes: Roll the die and move that many squares, from 1 up to 100. Land on the foot of a ladder to climb it, or on a snake’s head to slide down. From level 4 you must roll the exact number to land on 100. Higher levels have more snakes, fewer ladders and more opponents. First to reach 100 wins.
ui.lib.arcade.needExact: You need the exact number to land on 100.
ui.lib.arcade.note.nmm: Each side has 9 pieces. Phase 1: take turns placing pieces on empty points. Phase 2: slide a piece to an adjacent empty point. With only 3 pieces left you may “fly” to any empty point. Make three in a row (a “mill”) to remove an opponent’s piece (pieces not in a mill first). You lose when you are down to 2 pieces or cannot move. You play white and go first.
ui.lib.arcade.removePiece: Pick an opponent piece to remove.
ui.lib.arcade.note.battleship: Each side has 5 ships (lengths 5, 4, 3, 3, 2) placed at random on a 10x10 grid. Take turns firing at a cell: a hit turns red, a miss turns light blue, and hitting every cell of a ship sinks it. Sink the whole enemy fleet first to win. At higher levels the computer deduces your ships’ positions more cleverly.

ui.lib.arcade.note.bau-cua: Virtual coins only — no real money. Pick a chip value, click the animals to place bets, then press Shake. For every die that matches an animal you bet on, you get your stake back plus an equal amount for each match. Reach the target coins within the allowed rounds to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.baccarat: Virtual coins only — no real money. Bet on Player, Banker or Tie, then press Deal. A hand’s value is the last digit of its total (A = 1, 2–9 face value, 10/J/Q/K = 0); the hand closer to 9 wins, and third cards are drawn by the standard rules. Player pays 1:1, Banker 0.95:1, Tie 8:1 (Player/Banker bets are returned on a tie). Reach the target coins within the allowed rounds to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.bai-cao: Virtual coins only — no real money. Each side gets 3 cards. A hand scores the last digit of its total (A = 1, 2–9 face value, 10/J/Q/K = 10, i.e. 0 points). Ranking: Three of a kind (“Sáp”) is highest, then three face cards (“Ba tiên”), then 9 points down to 0. Place a bet, press Deal and then Reveal to compare with the dealer. From level 6 the dealer wins ties. Reach the target coins within the allowed rounds to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.bingo: The computer calls numbers from 1 to 75. When a called number is on your card, click it to mark it (the centre is free). Complete a row, column or diagonal and press BINGO! — you must beat the computer opponents. A false BINGO! locks the button for a few seconds. Higher levels call faster and have more opponents.
ui.lib.arcade.falseBingo: Not a full line yet! Button locked for 3 seconds.
ui.lib.arcade.note.yahtzee: Each turn you roll 5 dice up to 3 times: click a die to keep it, then press Roll to re-roll the others. Then pick a box in the table to score (each box is used once; a box that does not fit scores 0). 13 turns. The Ones–Sixes boxes add a 35 bonus if they total 63 or more. Reach the level’s target score to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.crazy-eights: Play a card that matches the top card of the discard pile by suit or rank. Eights are wild: play one any time and choose a new suit. If you have no playable card, draw from the pile (up to 3 cards); if you still cannot play, you pass. First to empty their hand wins. Higher levels have more opponents and the computer plays more cleverly.
ui.lib.arcade.mustPlay: You have a playable card — play it.
ui.lib.arcade.note.race: Press ← → (or tap the lane you want) to change lanes and dodge the cars ahead. You have 3 lives; drive the full distance to clear the level. Higher levels add lanes and faster traffic.
ui.lib.arcade.note.jump: The character bounces by itself. Press ← → or drag your finger to land on the next platform. Blue platforms move, brown ones break when you land. Falling off the screen loses; climb high enough to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.miner: The hook swings back and forth; press Space, ↓ or tap the field to drop it. Big gold and rocks are heavy and pull slowly; diamonds are worth a lot. Reach the target money before the 60 seconds run out.
ui.lib.arcade.note.slicer: Swipe a finger or the mouse across the fruit to slice it. Avoid the black bombs. Missing a fruit or slicing a bomb costs a life (you have 3). Slice enough fruit to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hoops: Press on the court, drag down (like a slingshot) and release to shoot the ball at the hoop. The farther you drag, the harder the throw. Score enough baskets within the shots you have; from level 4 the hoop moves.
ui.lib.arcade.note.bubbles: Move the mouse or finger to aim, then click/tap or press Space/Fire to shoot. Connect 3 or more bubbles of the same color to pop them; bubbles that lose their support fall. The rows slowly drop, so keep them away from the bottom line. Clear all bubbles to win.
ui.lib.arcade.note.chase: Use the arrow keys (or swipe / the buttons) to turn and eat every dot in the maze while avoiding the ghosts chasing you. You have 3 lives; higher levels add more ghosts that are faster and chase smarter.
ui.lib.arcade.note.kakuro: Fill the white cells with digits 1–9 so that each run adds up to the clue in the black cell (the number at the top right is for the run to the right, the one at the bottom left for the run below), with no digit repeated within a run. Use the arrow keys to move.
ui.lib.arcade.note.kenken: Fill the grid with the numbers 1 to N so that no number repeats in any row or column. Each heavily outlined cage shows a target and an operation (+, −, ×, ÷): the numbers in the cage must give that result. Use the arrow keys to move.
ui.lib.arcade.note.wordGuess: Guess the secret English word. After each try, green means the right letter in the right place, yellow means the letter is in the word but elsewhere, and gray means it is not in the word. Type on your keyboard or use the on-screen keys, and press Enter to submit. Higher levels have longer words and fewer tries.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hangman: Guess the secret English word by picking letters one at a time. Each wrong letter adds a part to the hanged figure; when you run out of wrong guesses you lose. Higher levels have longer words and fewer wrong guesses allowed.
ui.lib.arcade.note.scramble: Rearrange the scrambled letters into a real English word and type it in the answer box. Each level has 5 words; solve at least 4 before each word’s timer runs out to clear the level. The hint reveals the first letter.
ui.lib.arcade.note.domino: Each player gets 7 tiles; whoever holds the highest double starts. Play a tile whose number matches one end of the chain. If you cannot play, draw from the boneyard until you can; if it is empty, pass. First to empty their hand wins; if both are blocked, the lower pip total wins.
ui.lib.arcade.note.hearts: Four players, 13 cards each. The 2 of clubs leads. You must follow the suit led if you can. Each heart is 1 point and the Queen of Spades is 13; whoever wins a trick takes its points. Lower is better, and taking all 26 points gives everyone else 26 instead. You cannot lead a heart until one has been played. After the last hand, you win if your score is the lowest (or tied for lowest).
ui.lib.arcade.note.holdem: Heads-up against the computer using virtual chips only. Each player gets 2 private cards and 5 community cards are revealed (flop, turn, river); make the best 5-card hand. Each round you can fold, call (or check) or raise. The blinds rise every 4 hands. You win when the computer runs out of chips, or by having more chips after the hand limit. No real money is involved.
ui.lib.arcade.hrIllegal: You cannot play this card (follow the suit, or no hearts lead yet).
ui.lib.arcade.thOppFold: The computer folds; you win this hand.
ui.lib.arcade.note.nback: A square lights up one after another on a 3x3 grid. Press "Match!" (or Space) when the lit position is the same as the one N steps ago (N is shown above). You need at least 80% correct decisions to clear the level. Higher levels use a larger N.
ui.lib.arcade.note.clicker: Click the cookie to bake cookies, then spend them on helpers that bake automatically (prices rise with each one you buy). Bake the target number of cookies within 2 minutes to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.onet: Select two identical tiles that can be joined by a path with at most 2 turns that does not cross other tiles to remove them. Clear all the tiles before time runs out to win. When no moves are left you can shuffle (limited uses).
ui.lib.arcade.note.jigsaw: The picture is cut into pieces and shuffled. Tap one piece, then another, to swap them, and rebuild the picture shown as the reference. Pieces in the right place get a green border. Higher levels have more pieces.
ui.lib.arcade.note.backgammon: You play the white checkers, moving from the top right around to the bottom right (your home). Roll the dice, click the checker you want to move, then click a highlighted destination. Landing on a point with exactly one opposing checker hits it onto the middle bar, and that player must bring it back in first. You cannot land on a point with two or more opposing checkers. Once all 15 of your checkers are in your home board (the last 6 points) you may bear them off. The first to bear off all 15 wins.
ui.lib.arcade.youNoMove: You have no legal move left.
ui.lib.arcade.note.tienlen: Four players, 13 cards each. Card order from low to high: 3, 4, … K, A, 2; suits from low to high: spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts. Whoever holds the 3 of spades goes first. Play a single card, a pair, three of a kind, four of a kind, or a run of 3 or more consecutive cards (no 2s). The next player must play the same type and higher, or pass; four of a kind can beat a single 2 or a pair of 2s. When everyone else passes, the last player to play may lead anything. First to empty their hand wins. Select cards, then press Play.
ui.lib.arcade.tlFree: Table empty — you may lead anything
ui.lib.arcade.tlBad: The selected cards do not form a valid set.
ui.lib.arcade.tlLow: This set is not high enough to beat the table.
ui.lib.arcade.note.td: Tap an empty square (not the path) to build a shooting tower, which costs gold; tap a tower again to upgrade it (up to level 5). Towers automatically shoot the enemy that has gone farthest within range. Defeat enemies to earn more gold; if 15 enemies reach the end you lose. Survive every wave to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.colorNum: Every square has a number matching a color in the palette. Pick a color, then tap the squares with that number to paint them; tapping with the wrong color paints nothing. Paint every square correctly to finish the picture. Higher levels have more colors.
ui.lib.arcade.cnWrong: Wrong color — check the number on the square.
ui.lib.arcade.note.yukon: Like Klondike but with no stock: any face-up card can be moved together with every card on top of it, even if they are not in sequence; only the first card must fit the target column (descending, alternating red and black; a King goes to an empty column). Build all 52 cards up on the four foundations from Ace to King. Low levels start with more cards already face up.
ui.lib.arcade.note.chinesechk: You play the blue pieces in the right-hand corner; move all 10 of them to the opposite left-hand corner before the computer does. Each turn you move one piece: step to an empty neighbouring hole, or jump over any piece to the empty hole right behind it, and keep jumping as many times as you like. Tap one of your pieces, then tap a green hole to move.
ui.lib.arcade.ccDraw: Out of turns — it is a draw.
ui.lib.arcade.note.maubinh: You and the computer each get 13 cards and arrange them into 3 hands: a 5-card back hand, a 5-card middle hand and a 3-card front hand. The back hand must be at least as strong as the middle, and the middle at least as strong as the front; otherwise your arrangement is fouled and you lose the whole round. Tap a card, then tap the row where it goes (tap a placed card to take it back). Each hand you win scores 1 point; winning all 3 scores 6. Play 5 rounds — a positive total clears the level. The front hand can only be high card, a pair or three of a kind.
ui.lib.arcade.mbAutoMsg: Here is a suggested arrangement. You can change it before showing the cards.
ui.lib.arcade.note.phom: Two players; each gets 9 cards (whoever goes first gets 10). A meld is 3 or more cards of the same rank, or 3 or more consecutive cards of the same suit (Ace is only low). On your turn draw a card from the deck, or take the card your opponent just discarded if it forms a meld with your hand (a card you took must be kept), then discard one card. When each player has discarded 4 cards the round ends and whoever has the lower total of unmelded cards (Ace = 1 … King = 13) wins. If all your cards are in melds after a discard you go out ("U") and win at once. Cards outlined in green are in your best set of melds.
ui.lib.arcade.pmAte: You took this card — keep it in a meld.
ui.lib.arcade.pmKeep: A card you took must be kept — discard another.
ui.lib.arcade.note.shogi: Shogi is Japanese chess. You play the lower side and move first; the computer's pieces point the other way. Captured pieces go into your hand and can be dropped on any empty square instead of making a move (never a pawn in a file where you already have an unpromoted pawn, and never a piece on a rank where it could not move again). A piece that moves into, out of, or within the last three ranks of the opponent may promote (except King and Gold); promotion is forced when a piece would have no moves. Checkmate the enemy King to win. Kanji: 歩 pawn, 香 lance, 桂 knight, 銀 silver, 金 gold, 角 bishop, 飛 rook, 玉 king; と, 馬, 竜 and other red pieces are promoted.
ui.lib.arcade.note.janggi: Janggi is Korean chess. You play the blue pieces at the bottom and move first. Unlike xiangqi there is no river, and both palaces have diagonal lines. The General and Guards move one step along the palace lines (diagonals included); the Chariot also slides and captures along palace diagonals; the Cannon must jump over exactly one piece (not another Cannon) to move or capture, and cannot capture a Cannon; the Horse steps one point straight then one diagonally, and the Elephant one straight then two diagonally, both blocked if a piece is in the way; Soldiers move forward or sideways, and diagonally forward inside the enemy palace. The two Generals may never face each other. Checkmate the enemy General to win. The computer never passes.
ui.lib.arcade.note.pinball: Press Space, Up or tap the table to launch the ball. Hold Left (or touch the left half of the table) to raise the left flipper and Right (or the right half) for the right one — tap in rhythm instead of holding. Round bumpers score 100 points each. You have 3 balls; reach the target score before they run out to clear the level.
ui.lib.arcade.note.cribbage: Two-player cribbage, a race to 61 points. Each deal you get 6 cards and put 2 face down into the crib (it belongs to the dealer). A starter card is turned up. Then take turns playing cards face up with the running total never above 31: reaching 15 or 31 scores 2, matching the last card scores 2/6/12, a run of 3 or more (in any order) scores its length, and when nobody can play the last player scores 1 ("Go"). Then each hand of 4 is counted with the starter: every combination totalling 15 scores 2, each pair 2, a run of 3+ its length, four cards of one suit 4 (5 with the starter), and a Jack matching the starter suit 1. The non-dealer counts first, then the dealer counts their hand and the crib.
ui.lib.arcade.note.tangram: Fit all the pieces (only a few on low levels) exactly into the grey silhouette without overlapping. Drag a piece to move it; tap a piece to turn it 45°, or use the Rotate and Flip buttons (the parallelogram must be flipped the right way round). A piece dropped near a corner snaps to it. Levels 1–4 show dashed hint lines; the Hint button turns them on and off.

rsa-keys.note: Everything runs in your browser via Web Crypto and is never sent anywhere. Because RSA can only encrypt very short data directly, the tool uses hybrid encryption: it generates a random AES key to encrypt the text, then wraps that AES key with RSA — so text of any length can be encrypted. The recipient needs the matching private key to decrypt. The public key (SPKI) can be shared; the private key (PKCS#8) must be kept secret.

rsa-keys.err.pubRead: Could not read the public key. It needs the correct public PEM format (-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----, SPKI).
rsa-keys.err.privRead: Could not read the private key. It needs the correct private PEM format (-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----, PKCS#8).
rsa-keys.status.noPub: No public key, so cannot encrypt. Generate or paste a public key.

pit-tax.seo.howTitle: How personal income tax on salary is calculated
pit-tax.seo.how1: Yearly personal income tax is charged on taxable income: total taxable salary and bonuses, minus mandatory insurance, the personal deduction, the dependant deduction and donations to charity, humanitarian and education causes.
pit-tax.seo.how2: From tax year 2026 the deduction is 15.5 million dong per month for yourself and 6.2 million dong per month for each dependant. The progressive table has 5 brackets: 5%, 10%, 20%, 30% and 35% (yearly limits are the monthly limits multiplied by 12).
pit-tax.seo.how3: A Tet bonus or 13th-month salary is added to your yearly income, so the last part of your income can move into a higher bracket. The tool shows how much extra tax the bonus alone causes.
pit-tax.faq.q1: How is personal income tax on salary calculated for 2026?
pit-tax.faq.a1: Take your total taxable income for the year, subtract mandatory insurance, the personal deduction of 15.5 million dong per month, the dependant deduction of 6.2 million dong per month and other allowed deductions, then apply the 5-bracket progressive table.
pit-tax.faq.q2: When do I pay more tax or get a refund?
pit-tax.faq.a2: If the tax for the whole year is higher than the tax withheld each month, you pay the difference; if it is lower, you get a refund or credit it to the next period. Enter the tax already withheld to see the difference.
pit-tax.faq.a3: Yes. A Tet bonus is salary income, so it is added to the taxable income of the year and taxed on the progressive table together with your salary.
pit-tax.faq.q4: When is the deadline to finalize personal income tax?
pit-tax.faq.a4: Employers finalize on your behalf by 31 March at the latest, and individuals who file themselves must do so with the tax office by 30 April of the following year.
pit-tax.faq.a5: The result is a reference based on the rules stated. It does not cover special cases such as income from several employers, foreigners or non-salary income, so check with the tax office when you finalize.

savings-bhxh.seo.howTitle: How savings interest, pension and lump-sum social insurance are calculated
savings-bhxh.seo.how1: Interest on a fixed-term deposit equals the deposit times the yearly rate times the number of months divided by 12. You can take interest at maturity, take it every month, or roll principal and interest over so interest earns interest.
savings-bhxh.seo.how2: The monthly pension equals the pension rate times the average salary used for social insurance contributions. Under the Law on Social Insurance 2024, women with 15 years of contributions receive 45%; men with 15 years receive 40% and the rate rises with each extra year, up to a maximum of 75%.
savings-bhxh.seo.how3: The lump-sum payout is 1.5 months of average salary for each year contributed before 2014 and 2 months for each year contributed from 2014. Taking it gives up the contribution record you need for a pension and for health insurance later.
savings-bhxh.faq.q1: How much interest do I earn on 100 million dong for 12 months?
savings-bhxh.faq.a1: For a full 12 months the interest equals the deposit times the yearly rate. For example, at 6% a year the interest is 6 million dong. Enter your amount, term and the bank's rate for an exact result.
savings-bhxh.faq.q2: How is interest calculated if I withdraw early?
savings-bhxh.faq.a2: Most banks only pay the demand-deposit rate, usually very low, for the actual days deposited. The tool shows how much interest you lose compared with a full term.
savings-bhxh.faq.q3: How many years of contributions do I need for a pension?
savings-bhxh.faq.a3: Under the Law on Social Insurance 2024 you need at least 15 years of contributions and to reach retirement age. The maximum pension rate is 75% of the average salary used for contributions.
savings-bhxh.faq.q4: How is the lump-sum social insurance payout calculated?
savings-bhxh.faq.a4: Each year contributed before 2014 earns 1.5 months and each year from 2014 earns 2 months of average salary. Extra time of 1 to 6 months counts as half a year and 7 to 11 months as a full year.
savings-bhxh.faq.q5: Does the result replace the notice from the social insurance agency?
savings-bhxh.faq.a5: No. It is only an estimate based on the average salary you enter and does not include salary adjustment, early retirement or special cases. The official amount is set by the social insurance agency.

time-calc.dur.lines: One time span per line (hours:minutes:seconds). Add a minus sign to subtract.
time-calc.unix.dt: Or pick a date and time (your device time)
time-calc.work.errTime: Choose a start time and an end time.
time-calc.work.overnight: Overnight shift: the end time counts as the next day.
time-calc.lunar.none: This lunar date does not exist (check day 30 or the leap month).
time-calc.seo.howTitle: How time, work hours and calendar conversion are calculated
time-calc.seo.how1: The Add and subtract tab lets you enter several time spans as hours:minutes:seconds and add or subtract them, for example 1:30:00 + 0:45:30. The result is shown in hours, minutes and seconds, plus total minutes and decimal hours.
time-calc.seo.how2: The Work hours tab calculates the time between clock-in and clock-out, adds 24 hours when the shift passes midnight, subtracts the break and converts the result to decimal hours so you can multiply it by an hourly rate.
time-calc.seo.how3: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds (or milliseconds) since 00:00 UTC on 1 January 1970. The lunar calendar is converted with an astronomical algorithm for the Vietnam time zone (UTC+7), including leap months and the Can Chi (sexagenary) names of the year and day.
time-calc.faq.q1: How do I add up several hour:minute:second durations?
time-calc.faq.a1: Enter each span as hours:minutes:seconds or as 1h 30m on its own line, put a minus sign in front of the ones to subtract, and the total updates right away together with decimal hours.
time-calc.faq.q2: How is an overnight shift calculated?
time-calc.faq.a2: If the end time is earlier than the start time, the tool assumes the shift ends the next day, adds 24 hours and then subtracts the break.
time-calc.faq.q3: What is a Unix timestamp and what forms does it come in?
time-calc.faq.a3: It is the number of seconds since 1 January 1970 UTC. It comes as 10 digits (seconds) or 13 digits (milliseconds); the tool recognizes which one you paste.
time-calc.faq.q4: Is the solar to lunar conversion accurate?
time-calc.faq.a4: The tool uses an astronomical algorithm for new moons and solar terms in the Vietnam time zone (UTC+7), matching the common perpetual calendars, including leap months.
time-calc.faq.q5: Can I convert from the lunar calendar back to the solar calendar?
time-calc.faq.a5: Yes. Enter the lunar day, month and year, tick leap month if needed, and the tool returns the matching solar date.

todo-pomodoro.td.empty: No tasks in this view yet.
todo-pomodoro.seo.howTitle: How to use the to-do list and Pomodoro timer
todo-pomodoro.seo.how1: Add a task, choose a priority and a due date if you want one. Urgent and overdue tasks are shown first, and you can filter by tasks that are not done, done, or due today.
todo-pomodoro.seo.how2: The Pomodoro technique splits your time into focused work sessions, 25 minutes by default, separated by 5-minute short breaks. After 4 sessions you take a 15-minute long break. You can change all of these durations.
todo-pomodoro.seo.how3: Pick the task you are working on, and every completed focus session is counted for it. Your data is saved in your own browser and is not sent anywhere.
todo-pomodoro.faq.a1: A time management method: work with full focus for 25 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes. After four sessions you take a longer break. The name comes from the tomato-shaped kitchen timer.
todo-pomodoro.faq.q2: Can I change the length of each session?
todo-pomodoro.faq.a2: Yes. You can set the minutes for focus, short break and long break and the number of sessions before a long break; the settings are remembered for next time.
todo-pomodoro.faq.q3: Does the timer keep running if I switch tabs?
todo-pomodoro.faq.a3: The page needs to stay open so it can ring. It counts time using the system clock, so it does not fall behind when you move to another tab.
todo-pomodoro.faq.q4: Where is my task list stored?
todo-pomodoro.faq.a4: In your browser storage on this device and never on a server. If you clear browser data or switch devices, the list will not be there.
todo-pomodoro.faq.q5: Is there a notification when time is up?
todo-pomodoro.faq.a5: A short chime plays, and the remaining time is shown in the tab title so you can follow it while working in another window.

flashcards.importCsv: Import a CSV file or drop it here
flashcards.storeNote: Cards are stored in this browser and are not sent to a server. Export a CSV to back them up.
flashcards.confirmDelete: Delete this deck and all the cards in it?
flashcards.study.allDone: You have reviewed every card that was due. Well done!
flashcards.study.empty: This deck has no cards yet. Go to Cards in deck to add some.
flashcards.study.tap: Tap the card to flip it
flashcards.noSpeech: This browser does not support text to speech.
flashcards.quiz.need: You need at least 4 cards with different answers to take a quiz.
flashcards.noneAdded: No valid cards found. Each line needs two parts separated by a dash.
flashcards.needBoth: Enter both the front and the back.
flashcards.confirmReset: Reset the study progress of every card in this deck?
flashcards.seo.how1: Create a deck by pasting several lines in the form "front - back" or by adding cards one at a time. You can also import a CSV file and export it again to back it up or use it elsewhere.
flashcards.seo.how2: While studying, tap the card to flip it and see the answer, then choose Got it or Not yet. A card you remembered moves to a higher box and is scheduled further out; a card you forgot goes back to the first box to be reviewed again right away.
flashcards.seo.how3: Quiz mode builds four-choice questions from your own deck. The listen button reads the card aloud with your browser voice, and you can choose the language.
flashcards.faq.q1: How do flashcards help with learning vocabulary?
flashcards.faq.a1: Trying to recall the answer before flipping the card strengthens memory more than simply rereading. Reviewing at growing intervals helps you remember for longer in less time.
flashcards.faq.q2: What is the Leitner box system?
flashcards.faq.a2: It sorts cards into boxes. A card you remember moves up a box and is reviewed less often, after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 days; a card you forget goes back to the first box.
flashcards.faq.q3: How do I import a list of words I already have?
flashcards.faq.a3: Paste lines made of two parts separated by a dash, a colon, a semicolon or a Tab, or choose a two-column CSV file.
flashcards.faq.a4: In your browser, never on a server. Export a CSV to back it up before you clear browser data or change devices.
flashcards.faq.q5: How does the pronunciation feature work?
flashcards.faq.a5: It uses the voice built into your browser or operating system. Choose the deck language so the right voice is used; some languages need the matching voice to be installed on your device.

media-trim-convert.dropTitle: Choose an audio or video file, or drop it here
media-trim-convert.dropHint: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG… Up to 1 GB.
media-trim-convert.fast: Fast trim, keeps the original quality (the cut point may be off by a few seconds)
media-trim-convert.note: Processed in your browser with ffmpeg, so your file is not uploaded to a server. The first run downloads the processor, about 31 MB. Only process files you have the right to use.
media-trim-convert.needVideo: This action needs a video file.
media-trim-convert.tooBig: The file is larger than 1 GB and the browser does not have enough memory to process it.
media-trim-convert.badTime: Invalid time. Use minutes:seconds, for example 1:30; the end must be after the start.
media-trim-convert.gifLong: A GIF should be shorter than 60 seconds. Choose a shorter part.
media-trim-convert.failed: This file could not be processed. It may be damaged or in an unsupported format.
media-trim-convert.seo.howTitle: How to trim and convert audio and video
media-trim-convert.seo.how1: Choose a file, preview it, then enter the start and end points or use the current player position. Fast trim keeps the original quality and is very quick, but the cut point may be off by a few seconds; precise trimming re-encodes the file.
media-trim-convert.seo.how2: The Convert format tab turns video into MP4 or WebM, and turns audio, or the sound track of a video, into MP3, M4A, WAV or OGG, with three quality levels.
media-trim-convert.seo.how3: The Video to GIF tab makes an animated image from part of a video, with a choice of frames per second and width. Everything uses ffmpeg running inside your browser, so your files are never sent anywhere.
media-trim-convert.faq.q1: Does trimming a video reduce its quality?
media-trim-convert.faq.a1: Fast trim copies the data as it is, so quality is unchanged. Precise trim re-encodes the video, so quality depends on the level you choose.
media-trim-convert.faq.q2: Why is the fast trim point a little off?
media-trim-convert.faq.a2: Fast trim can only cut at the video keyframes, so the clip may start slightly earlier. Use precise trim when you need an exact second.
media-trim-convert.faq.q3: Is my file uploaded to a server?
media-trim-convert.faq.a3: No. All processing happens in your browser. The first time, it downloads the ffmpeg processor, about 31 MB, and later your browser reuses it.
media-trim-convert.faq.q4: What is the file size limit?
media-trim-convert.faq.a4: Up to 1 GB, but big files need a lot of memory and run slowly. For long videos, trim first or use a computer instead of a phone.
media-trim-convert.faq.q5: Which format should I convert to?
media-trim-convert.faq.a5: MP4 plays on almost every device, WebM is light for the web, MP3 is the most common audio format, and WAV is uncompressed so it keeps original quality but is large.

base64-text.sample: Hello WFTools! This tool runs right in your browser.
base64-text.decNote: Automatically detects standard Base64, Base64URL (using - and _) and data:...;base64, strings, with or without = padding.
base64-text.binary: (Binary data, not text. Click "Save as file" to download it)
base64-text.bad: This is not a valid Base64 string. Check for stray characters or a truncated part.
base64-text.seo.howTitle: What is Base64 and how to use this tool
base64-text.seo.how1: Base64 represents any data using 64 safe characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, + and /). It is commonly used to embed images in HTML/CSS, send email attachments or carry binary data inside JSON.
base64-text.seo.how2: The Encode tab converts text to Base64 using UTF-8, so accented and non-English characters come through intact. Choose Base64URL when the string goes into a link or a JWT token.
base64-text.seo.how3: The Decode tab automatically handles strings with or without = padding and data URIs. If the result is binary data, you can save it as a file.
base64-text.faq.q1: Is Base64 a form of secure encryption?
base64-text.faq.a1: No. Base64 is just a way of rewriting data, and anyone can decode it. To keep data secret, use the AES Encryption tool.
base64-text.faq.q2: Why is a Base64 string longer than the original text?
base64-text.faq.a2: Every 3 bytes of data are written as 4 characters, so the size grows by about 33%.
base64-text.faq.q3: How is Base64URL different from standard Base64?
base64-text.faq.a3: Base64URL replaces + with - and / with _, and usually drops the trailing = so it is safe in links and file names.
base64-text.faq.q4: What if the decoded text looks garbled?
base64-text.faq.a4: The original data may not be UTF-8, or it may be a binary file. Click Save as file and open it with the right program.
base64-text.faq.q5: Is there a file size limit?
base64-text.faq.a5: There is no fixed limit, but files over a few dozen MB may slow down your browser because everything is processed in your device's memory.

url-encode.note: Type in the left box to encode, or paste a string containing %XX into the right box and click Decode. Accented characters are converted to UTF-8.
url-encode.bad: The string contains an invalid % character (it must be % followed by 2 hex digits, such as %20). Fix the problem and try again.
url-encode.seo.how1: Links can only contain certain characters. Accented letters, spaces, & or ? inside a parameter value must be converted to percent form such as %20 so browsers and servers understand them correctly.
url-encode.seo.how2: Component mode is for parameter values (after the = sign). Full URL mode keeps structural characters such as : / ? & # unchanged.
url-encode.seo.how3: Form data mode turns spaces into + signs, the same way a browser submits a form as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
url-encode.faq.q1: What is the difference between %20 and the + sign?
url-encode.faq.a1: Both mean a space. %20 works in any part of a URL, while + only means a space in a form query string.
url-encode.faq.q2: Why does my link turn into something like %C3%A9?
url-encode.faq.a2: Browsers encode accented characters as UTF-8, turning each one into 2 to 3 %XX groups. Paste that string into the right box and click Decode to read it again.
url-encode.faq.q3: Should I use encodeURI or encodeURIComponent?
url-encode.faq.a3: Use encodeURIComponent for each parameter value, and encodeURI for a whole link when you only want to convert accented letters and spaces.
url-encode.faq.q4: What does the invalid % error mean when decoding?
url-encode.faq.a4: The string has a % sign that is not followed by exactly 2 hex digits, for example 50%. Change it to %25 or remove the stray % sign.
url-encode.faq.q5: Is the data I paste sent anywhere?
url-encode.faq.a5: No. Encoding and decoding run entirely in JavaScript on your device.

hash-gen.fileNote: Use this to check whether a downloaded file matches the hash published by its vendor.
hash-gen.match: Matches {a}. The file or text is exactly as published.
hash-gen.noMatch: No algorithm matches. The data has been changed, or you are comparing against the wrong algorithm.
hash-gen.seo.how1: A hash function turns any data into a string of fixed length. Change a single character and the hash changes completely, so it is used to check whether a file was corrupted or altered during download.
hash-gen.seo.how2: Software vendors often publish a SHA-256 hash next to the download. Choose the file on the Hash file tab, paste the published hash into the compare box, and the tool tells you right away whether they match.
hash-gen.seo.how3: MD5 and SHA-1 are no longer safe against deliberate forgery, but they still work well for catching transfer errors. When security matters, use SHA-256 or stronger.
hash-gen.faq.q1: Can a hash be reversed to the original text?
hash-gen.faq.a1: No. Hashing is one-way. Sites that claim to decrypt MD5 simply look the hash up in a database of common passwords that were hashed in advance.
hash-gen.faq.q2: Is a large file uploaded when I hash it?
hash-gen.faq.a2: No. The file is read and hashed right in your browser, even files of several GB (depending on your device memory).
hash-gen.faq.q3: Why is my result different from another machine?
hash-gen.faq.a3: Check for spaces, trailing line breaks and the character encoding. This tool hashes strings as UTF-8.
hash-gen.faq.q4: Should I store passwords with MD5 or SHA-256?
hash-gen.faq.a4: No. Passwords need a slow, salted algorithm such as bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2.
hash-gen.faq.q5: How is CRC32 different from SHA?
hash-gen.faq.a5: CRC32 is very fast and only 8 characters long. It is used to detect random errors (ZIP files, networks), not for security.

jwt-decode.bad: This is not a JWT: it must have 3 parts separated by dots (xxx.yyy.zzz).
jwt-decode.badJson: The header or payload could not be decoded as JSON. The token may have been cut off when copied.
jwt-decode.algNo: This token uses the {a} algorithm: only HMAC signatures (HS256/384/512) can be verified, using a secret key.
jwt-decode.sigOk: The signature is valid for this key.
jwt-decode.sigBad: The signature does not match: the secret key is wrong or the token has been altered.
jwt-decode.seo.how1: A JWT has 3 parts separated by dots: the header (algorithm), the payload (user info, permissions, expiry) and the signature. The first two are just JSON written in Base64URL, so anyone can read them.
jwt-decode.seo.how2: This tool decodes the first two parts, formats them neatly and converts the exp, iat and nbf timestamps into readable dates and times, along with whether the token is still valid or expired.
jwt-decode.seo.how3: For tokens signed with HMAC (HS256, HS384, HS512), enter the secret key to check that the signature is valid, meaning the token was not altered and was truly issued by your server.
jwt-decode.faq.q1: Is it safe to paste a real token here?
jwt-decode.faq.a1: The token is processed entirely in your browser and never sent anywhere. Even so, do not share a live token with others, because it may let them sign in as you.
jwt-decode.faq.q2: Why can anyone read the payload?
jwt-decode.faq.a2: The payload is only Base64URL-encoded, not encrypted. Never put passwords or sensitive data in a JWT.
jwt-decode.faq.a3: exp is the expiry time in seconds since January 1, 1970 (Unix time). After this moment the server must reject the token.
jwt-decode.faq.q4: Can I verify an RS256 token?
jwt-decode.faq.a4: The tool can read the contents of RS256 and ES256 tokens, but it only verifies signatures for HMAC algorithms that use a shared secret key.
jwt-decode.faq.q5: The tool says the token cannot be decoded. Why?
jwt-decode.faq.a5: It is usually caused by missing characters or by extra text such as Bearer or quotation marks when copying. The tool removes a leading Bearer automatically.

html-entities.m.all: Convert all non-ASCII characters to numeric codes (é)
html-entities.note: Encoding lets you show HTML code as plain text on a web page (so the browser does not run it). Decoding turns &lt; &#233; … back into real characters.
html-entities.seo.how1: An HTML entity is a way to write a character as a code, for example < for the < sign or © for ©. This lets you display HTML code on a web page without the browser running it.
html-entities.seo.how2: Basic mode converts only the 5 characters that have special meaning in HTML. Named entity mode also converts common symbols such as € ™ — into readable names.
html-entities.seo.how3: Numeric mode converts every non-ASCII character, including accented letters, into &#number; form, so it works even on legacy systems that do not support UTF-8.
html-entities.faq.q1: When do I need to encode entities?
html-entities.faq.a1: When putting user-entered content on a web page, writing tutorials that include HTML code, or inserting text into HTML attributes.
html-entities.faq.a2: Encoding the 5 characters & < > double quote and single quote is an important step against code injection, but it depends on context (inside scripts and URLs you need other methods).
html-entities.faq.a3: It is a non-breaking space, which keeps two words on the same line.
html-entities.faq.q4: Do I need to encode accented letters?
html-entities.faq.a4: Not if your page uses UTF-8. Only encode them when the target system does not support UTF-8.
html-entities.faq.q5: Does decoding support the hex form A?
html-entities.faq.a5: Yes. The tool decodes named entities, decimal numbers like A and hex like A.

uuid-gen.inspect: Paste a UUID/ULID to inspect it
uuid-gen.notId: Not a UUID (32 hex digits) or ULID (26 characters).
uuid-gen.seo.howTitle: Choosing the right kind of identifier
uuid-gen.seo.how1: A UUID is a 128-bit ID made of 32 hex digits, with a practically zero chance of collision. UUID v4 is completely random, which suits order IDs, session IDs and primary keys.
uuid-gen.seo.how2: UUID v7 and ULID put the creation time at the front, so they sort in time order, which helps databases write faster when used as primary keys.
uuid-gen.seo.how3: Paste an ID into the inspect box to see which UUID version it is and, for UUID v7 or ULID, when it was created.
uuid-gen.faq.a1: In theory yes, but with UUID v4 you would need to generate about 2.7 quintillion IDs to have a 50% chance of a single duplicate pair.
uuid-gen.faq.q2: Should I use UUID v4 or v7?
uuid-gen.faq.a2: Use v7 for database primary keys so indexes stay compact and fast. Use v4 when you do not want to reveal the creation time.
uuid-gen.faq.a3: A ULID is a 26-character ID (Crockford Base32 alphabet) whose first 10 characters are a timestamp. It is shorter and easier to read than a UUID.
uuid-gen.faq.a4: GUID is Microsoft's name for UUID. The format is the same, often written in uppercase and wrapped in curly braces.
uuid-gen.faq.a5: Yes. The tool uses your browser's crypto.getRandomValues, the same randomness source used for encryption.

aes-encrypt.pwNote: Remember your password: there is no way to recover the data if you forget it. Use a long, hard-to-guess password.
aes-encrypt.sample: Secret note: the safe combination is 2468.
aes-encrypt.algo: Algorithm: AES-256-GCM, with the key derived from your password using PBKDF2-SHA256 at 200,000 iterations, and a random salt and IV for every encryption.
aes-encrypt.wrong: Decryption failed: the password is wrong, or the data was not encrypted by this tool or has been altered.
aes-encrypt.seo.how1: Your password is stretched into a 256-bit key using PBKDF2-SHA256 over 200,000 iterations with a random salt, which makes password guessing extremely slow.
aes-encrypt.seo.how2: Data is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, the standard used by banks and messaging apps. GCM also detects if even a single byte of the data has been altered.
aes-encrypt.seo.how3: Encrypted text is output as Base64 so you can paste it into emails and messages. Files are saved with the .wftenc extension and decrypted again with this same tool.
aes-encrypt.faq.q1: Can I recover my data if I forget the password?
aes-encrypt.faq.a1: No. There is no back door, and we cannot open it either. Remember the password or store it in a password manager.
aes-encrypt.faq.q2: Is it safe to send encrypted text by email or chat?
aes-encrypt.faq.a2: Yes, as long as the password is strong and you share the password through a different channel (a phone call or in person).
aes-encrypt.faq.q3: Is it a bug that the result is different every time?
aes-encrypt.faq.a3: It is not a bug. The random salt and IV make the output different each time, but decryption still gives back the same content.
aes-encrypt.faq.a4: Yes, but files are processed in memory, so keep them under a few hundred MB on a phone.
aes-encrypt.faq.q5: Can I open a .wftenc file with other software?
aes-encrypt.faq.a5: The format is 4 bytes of WFT1, a 16-byte salt, a 12-byte IV, then the AES-GCM data. Developers can decrypt it themselves with standard libraries.

hmac-gen.use: HMAC is commonly used to verify webhooks (Stripe, GitHub, Shopify, payment gateways): the sender signs the content with a shared key, and the receiver signs it again and compares.
hmac-gen.badKey: The key does not match the chosen format (hex contains only 0-9, a-f).
hmac-gen.match: Match: the content is intact and came from a party holding the key.
hmac-gen.noMatch: No match: wrong key, wrong algorithm, or the content has been altered.
hmac-gen.seo.how1: HMAC is a signature created from a message and a shared secret key. The receiver signs the message again with the same key. If the two signatures match, the message was not altered and came from the right sender.
hmac-gen.seo.how2: Services such as Stripe, GitHub, Shopify and payment gateways sign their webhooks with HMAC. Paste the exact body you received and the key here to test.
hmac-gen.seo.how3: Choose the key format (text, hex, Base64) and output format exactly as the service documentation requires, because the wrong format produces a completely different signature.
hmac-gen.faq.q1: Why doesn't my signature match the service's?
hmac-gen.faq.a1: It is usually because whitespace in the body changed, the JSON field order changed, or the algorithm or hex/Base64 format is wrong. You must sign the exact original string you received.
hmac-gen.faq.q2: How is HMAC different from a SHA-256 hash?
hmac-gen.faq.a2: Anyone can compute SHA-256, but HMAC needs a secret key, so only someone holding the key can produce the correct signature.
hmac-gen.faq.q3: Is my secret key exposed when I paste it here?
hmac-gen.faq.a3: No. All calculations run in your browser using Web Crypto and nothing is sent anywhere.
hmac-gen.faq.q4: How do I compare a GitHub signature with the sha256= prefix?
hmac-gen.faq.a4: Paste the whole string into the compare box. The tool automatically removes the sha256= prefix when comparing.
hmac-gen.faq.a5: Only when a legacy system requires it. For new systems, use HMAC-SHA256 or stronger.

cipher-tools.note: Caesar, ROT13, Vigenère and Atbash only change the letters A-Z and leave numbers and punctuation unchanged. Morse strips accents before encoding. These ciphers are for learning and puzzles, and are not secure enough to protect real data.
cipher-tools.bad: Cannot decode: the data is not in the format of the selected cipher.
cipher-tools.seo.how1: The Caesar cipher shifts each letter by a number of steps in the alphabet, and ROT13 is a Caesar shift of 13. Vigenère uses a keyword so each letter shifts by a different amount, making it harder to guess.
cipher-tools.seo.how2: Morse code represents letters with dots and dashes, with words separated by /. Accented letters are converted to plain letters before encoding.
cipher-tools.seo.how3: Binary and hex convert each UTF-8 byte of the text into a string of 0s and 1s or into hexadecimal, which is handy when learning computer science basics.
cipher-tools.faq.a1: No. There are only 25 possible shifts, so all of them can be tried in seconds. Use it only for games and scouting-style secret messages.
cipher-tools.faq.q2: How do I decode a Caesar cipher when I don't know the shift?
cipher-tools.faq.a2: Try shifts from 1 to 25 in the Shift amount box until the text makes sense.
cipher-tools.faq.q3: What separates words in Morse code?
cipher-tools.faq.a3: Letters are separated by one space, and words by a / (or three spaces).
cipher-tools.faq.q4: Why do accents disappear in Morse code?
cipher-tools.faq.a4: International Morse has no accented letters, so the tool converts them to unaccented letters.
cipher-tools.faq.q5: Is there a cipher that is safe for real use?

unicode-inspect.warnNfc: The text contains decomposed accented letters (NFD). It is best to normalize it to NFC.
unicode-inspect.seo.how1: Strings that look identical can contain hidden characters such as a zero-width space (U+200B) or text direction marks, causing failed logins, searches that find nothing or strange source code errors.
unicode-inspect.seo.how2: Accented letters can be stored in two ways: precomposed (NFC) and decomposed (NFD, a base letter plus a separate accent mark). Text copied from macOS or PDFs is often NFD, so normalize it to NFC.
unicode-inspect.seo.how3: The stats show visible characters, code points, JavaScript length and UTF-8 bytes, so you can check database length limits, SMS or tweet limits.
unicode-inspect.faq.q1: Why is the string length different from the number of characters I see?
unicode-inspect.faq.a1: Emoji and some characters take 2 UTF-16 units or are made of several combined code points, so different ways of counting give different results.
unicode-inspect.faq.q2: Where do hidden characters come from?
unicode-inspect.faq.a2: Usually from copying out of web pages, Word, PDFs or chat apps. Click Remove hidden characters to clean the text.
unicode-inspect.faq.q3: Does NFC normalization change the content?
unicode-inspect.faq.a3: It does not change the visible text, only how it is stored, so programs compare and search it accurately.
unicode-inspect.faq.q4: How many bytes does an accented letter take?
unicode-inspect.faq.a4: Usually 2 to 3 bytes in UTF-8, while plain unaccented letters take just 1 byte.
unicode-inspect.faq.a5: The detail table shows up to the first 2,000 characters, but the stats are still calculated on the entire text.

string-escape.bad: The string has an escape sequence that is invalid for this context. Check for a missing \ or quote.
string-escape.seo.how1: In source code some characters have special meaning: a quote ends a string, a \ starts a special character, and a line break ends a line. Escaping writes them in a special way so the content stays intact.
string-escape.seo.how2: Choose the right context because each language has its own rules: SQL doubles single quotes, CSV wraps cells in double quotes, and Regex adds \ before . * + ? and brackets.
string-escape.seo.how3: The Unescape button does the reverse, turning strings from logs, JSON files or source code back into the original text.
string-escape.faq.q1: Does escaping a SQL string prevent SQL injection?
string-escape.faq.a1: It helps avoid syntax errors, but the safest approach is still to use parameterized statements (prepared statements).
string-escape.faq.q2: Why do Windows paths need two backslashes?
string-escape.faq.a2: In JSON and JavaScript a single \ starts a special character, so you must write \\ to get one real backslash.
string-escape.faq.a3: When you want to match a string that contains characters such as . or ( ) literally, without them taking on special meaning.
string-escape.faq.q4: How is a shell command escaped?
string-escape.faq.a4: The string is wrapped in single quotes, and any single quote inside is written by closing the string, adding an escaped quote and reopening it.
string-escape.faq.a5: Yes. When unescaping JavaScript style, the tool understands \uXXXX, \u{...} and \xXX.

json-to-types.note: Fields that appear in only some array items are marked optional, and null values make that field nullable. Integers and floating-point numbers are distinguished when the target language has both types.
json-to-types.seo.howTitle: How the tool infers data types
json-to-types.seo.how1: The tool reads each value in the JSON: string, integer, float, boolean, array and nested object, then creates a separate type for every child object, named after the field.
json-to-types.seo.how2: For arrays with many items, the objects are merged: fields present in only some items are marked optional, and fields with null values are marked nullable.
json-to-types.seo.how3: The output is a good starting point. You should review type names, date types (which are left as strings) and fields that can hold multiple types.
json-to-types.faq.q1: Does it support very large JSON?
json-to-types.faq.a1: Yes, but a representative sample is all you need. JSON of a few MB still runs fine on a computer.
json-to-types.faq.q2: Why is a date field a string?
json-to-types.faq.a2: JSON has no date type, so dates are always strings. You can change them to Date or time.Time afterward.
json-to-types.faq.q3: What is a Zod schema for?
json-to-types.faq.a3: Zod validates data at runtime (for example API responses) and infers the TypeScript type from the same definition.
json-to-types.faq.q4: How are field names with spaces handled?
json-to-types.faq.a4: TypeScript puts the name in quotes. Go and C# convert it to PascalCase and keep the original name in the json tag.
json-to-types.faq.q5: What type is an empty array?
json-to-types.faq.a5: An empty array doesn't give enough information, so the element type is unknown/any. Add a sample element.

json-viewer.seo.how2: JSONPath is like an address for data: $ is the root, .name is a field, [0] is the first item, [*] is every item, .. searches at any depth, and [?(@.price<35)] filters by a condition.
json-viewer.seo.how3: The Pretty-print button indents the JSON, and the Sort keys A-Z button makes it easier to compare two JSON documents.

json-viewer.faq.q3: Where does the JSON error point?

json-viewer.faq.q5: Can I open very large JSON files?

yaml-json-toml.note: TOML can only hold a table (object) at the top level and has no null values. Data that doesn't fit will show an error with the reason. Comments (#) are not preserved when converting.
yaml-json-toml.tomlRoot: TOML requires the root data to be an object (table), not an array or a single value.
yaml-json-toml.seo.how1: JSON is strict and widely used in APIs. YAML is easy to read thanks to indentation and is popular in Docker Compose, Kubernetes and GitHub Actions. TOML is explicit and table-based, used by Cargo (Rust), pyproject (Python) and Hugo.
yaml-json-toml.seo.how2: Choose the source and target formats and the result updates as you type. The Swap direction button moves the result into the input so you can convert back.
yaml-json-toml.seo.how3: TOML has no null value and requires a table at the root, so null fields are dropped when converting to TOML. Comments in YAML/TOML are not preserved.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q1: What does a YAML indentation error mean?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a1: YAML uses spaces to show nesting. Tabs are not allowed, and items at the same level must line up.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q2: Is data lost when converting YAML to JSON?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a2: No data is lost. Only comments are dropped, and anchors (&, *) are expanded into concrete values.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q3: Why does yes/no in YAML become true/false?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a3: The library follows the YAML 1.2 standard, so yes/no stay as strings. Only true/false are booleans.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q4: Do I need an internet connection to run it?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a4: The first time, the tool loads the js-yaml and smol-toml libraries from a CDN. After that, everything is processed on your device.
yaml-json-toml.faq.q5: Are TOML dates and times preserved?
yaml-json-toml.faq.a5: TOML dates and times are converted to ISO strings when converting to JSON/YAML.

sql-format.seo.how1: SQL written on a single line or generated by software is very hard to read. The tool puts each clause (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY) on its own line, with each column and each AND/OR condition on a separate line.
sql-format.seo.how2: Subqueries in parentheses are indented one extra level, and JOIN types start their own lines. Quoted strings and comments are preserved.
sql-format.seo.how3: The Minify to one line button removes comments and extra whitespace, which is handy for pasting into source code or logs.
sql-format.faq.q1: Does formatting change the query result?
sql-format.faq.a1: No. Only whitespace and the letter case of keywords change. Table names, column names and values stay the same.
sql-format.faq.a2: The tool handles common SQL syntax. Vendor-specific statements (stored procedures, PL/SQL) still get basic line breaks.
sql-format.faq.a3: It's not required, but it is a common convention that helps distinguish keywords from table and column names.
sql-format.faq.q4: Does it check SQL syntax errors?
sql-format.faq.a4: No. The tool only formats. Run the query against your database to check for errors.
sql-format.faq.q5: Is the data in my statement sent anywhere?
sql-format.faq.a5: No. Formatting happens in your browser.

cron-gen.expr: Cron expression (minute hour day month weekday)
cron-gen.never: This expression never runs (for example, February 31).
cron-gen.bad: Invalid expression. It needs 5 parts separated by spaces: minute (0-59) hour (0-23) day (1-31) month (1-12) weekday (0-6, 0 = Sunday). Use * , - / such as */5 or 1-5.
cron-gen.seo.how1: A cron expression has 5 parts separated by spaces: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12) and day of week (0-6, where 0 is Sunday). An asterisk * means every value.
cron-gen.seo.how2: Use commas for lists (1,15), hyphens for ranges (1-5) and a slash for steps (*/15 means every 15 minutes). You can also use English abbreviations such as MON-FRI and JAN.
cron-gen.seo.how3: The tool calculates the next 10 runs so you can be sure the schedule is right before putting it into crontab, GitHub Actions, a Kubernetes CronJob or a service scheduler.
cron-gen.faq.q1: Which time zone does cron use?
cron-gen.faq.a1: The time zone of the server running cron. GitHub Actions uses UTC, so 9 AM Eastern Standard Time (UTC-5) is 0 14 * * *.
cron-gen.faq.q2: What if I set both day of month and day of week?
cron-gen.faq.a2: Under the Unix cron rule, the job runs when either condition matches, not both.
cron-gen.faq.q3: How do I run a job every 30 seconds?
cron-gen.faq.a3: Standard cron has a minimum of 1 minute. For 30 seconds you need two entries, with the second one using sleep 30.
cron-gen.faq.q5: Does it support 6-field cron with seconds?
cron-gen.faq.a5: The tool uses standard Unix 5-field cron. Quartz and Spring add a seconds field at the start.

number-base.note: Type in any box and the others convert automatically. Supports very large numbers (unlimited digits), negative numbers and the prefixes 0x, 0b, 0o. You can use _ or spaces to group digits.
number-base.overflow: The value is outside the {b}-bit range.
number-base.bad: Contains a digit that is invalid for base {b}. For example, binary only has 0 and 1, and hex has 0-9 and A-F.
number-base.seo.how1: Computers store everything as binary numbers (0 and 1). Hexadecimal (hex) is more compact, with each digit equal to 4 bits, so it is widely used for color codes, memory addresses and hashes.
number-base.seo.how2: Type in any box and the others update instantly. The tool uses BigInt integers, so there is no limit on the number of digits, and it accepts the prefixes 0x, 0b and 0o.
number-base.seo.how3: Two's complement shows how computers store negative numbers in 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits, which is useful when learning embedded programming and assembly.
number-base.faq.q1: How do I convert decimal to binary by hand?
number-base.faq.a1: Keep dividing the number by 2 and write down the remainders, then read the remainders from bottom to top.
number-base.faq.q2: Why does hex use the letters A-F?
number-base.faq.a2: Base 16 needs 16 digits. After 0-9, the letters A-F represent 10 to 15.
number-base.faq.a3: It is a way to store negative numbers: invert every bit of the positive number and add 1. For example, -1 in 8 bits is 11111111.
number-base.faq.a4: Not yet. The tool only converts integers.
number-base.faq.a5: It is used to shorten numbers into short strings, such as short link codes and order numbers.

curl-convert.noUrl: No URL was found in the command.
curl-convert.quote: The command has an unclosed quote. Check for a missing ' or ".
curl-convert.seo.howTitle: How to convert cURL to code
curl-convert.seo.how1: cURL is a command for sending HTTP requests that is common in API documentation. The tool reads the method, URL, headers (-H), body (-d, --json), form data (-F) and credentials (-u), then rewrites them in the language you choose.
curl-convert.seo.how2: JSON bodies are recognized and written as clean objects (JSON.stringify, json= in Python). The -u credentials are converted into a Basic Authorization header.
curl-convert.seo.how3: Tip: open developer tools (F12) → Network, right-click a request → Copy → Copy as cURL (bash), then paste it here to recreate that exact request.
curl-convert.faq.q1: Does it support multi-line cURL commands with \?
curl-convert.faq.a1: Yes. A \ at the end of a line is joined automatically.
curl-convert.faq.q2: Does Copy as cURL from Windows (cmd) work?
curl-convert.faq.a2: Choose the bash version. The cmd version uses ^ for escaping, so it may be misread.
curl-convert.faq.q3: Is the token in my command sent anywhere?
curl-convert.faq.a3: No. The conversion runs in your browser. Even so, don't share code that contains a real token.
curl-convert.faq.q4: Calling an API with fetch from the browser gives a CORS error. Why?
curl-convert.faq.a4: That is a limit set by the API server, not a bug in the code. Call it from a server (Node.js) or enable CORS on the API side.
curl-convert.faq.a5: Display and network options such as -o, -w, --max-time and -x have no effect in code, so they are ignored.

json-diff.same: The two JSON documents have identical content.
json-diff.seo.how1: A plain text comparison reports differences just because keys were reordered or whitespace changed. This tool parses the JSON into data and compares key by key, so it only reports real differences in content.
json-diff.seo.how2: Each difference has a path such as $.settings.theme, the type of change (added, removed, value changed, type changed) and the values on both sides, color-coded for readability.

json-diff.faq.q1: Are different key orders treated as a difference?

json-diff.faq.q2: Are the number 1 and the string 1 different?
json-diff.faq.a2: Yes, that is reported as a type change.
json-diff.faq.q3: What is it used for in practice?
json-diff.faq.a3: Comparing API responses between two versions, config files between test and production environments, and data before and after processing.
json-diff.faq.a4: Yes. The Copy report button gives a table-style list you can paste into Excel or a message.

meta-tags.faq.q2: Why doesn't Facebook show my new image when I share?

meta-tags.faq.q3: Does the meta keywords tag still matter?
